title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with a synthetic video call, in which a face and voice were generated to stand in for a public figure. The fraud did not depend on breaching any system. It worked because the target treated a WhatsApp video call as sufficient proof that the person on screen was the Chief Minister, and the deployment that mattered was the ordinary consumer channel, not a platform the state or the company controlled.

The failure sits at the point of identity verification. Nothing in the call established that the speaker was who he appeared to be, and the escalating demands for fees, an unlock payment and a fine were the standard structure of an advance-fee scam. Catching it would have required a check outside the call itself, such as contacting the Chief Minister's office or the police through a number the victim already trusted, rather than any improvement to the deepfake.

It is not established who made the call, whether the face was generated from public footage, or whether the case has led to any arrest or charge. A registered case is not a finding of guilt, and the reporting does not show intent beyond the fraud itself.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would arrange the transfer. Giri was then asked to pay fees, including Rs 5,000 as exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN.

A person claiming to be a CBI officer then demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh in total before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand and realizing he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline and Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act.
